feed.title: AI Wiki — Research Papers
feed.subtitle: New arXiv papers, triaged for relevance and summarised to key points.

entry.title: Unlocking Lossless Speedups in LLMs via Discrete Diffusion
entry.summary:
Uno introduces diffusion-augmented LLMs that decouple standard autoregressive weights from lightweight diffusion weights to enable parallel, lossless token generation without a draft model.

Why it matters: It enables significant parallel inference acceleration for standard AR language models while preserving baseline generation quality and eliminating draft model overhead.

entry.title: UniMate: One Unified Model to Animate Diverse Skeletons
entry.summary:
UniMate is a topology-aware diffusion transformer that generates motion for arbitrary 3D skeletons from a text prompt and rest pose without per-skeleton fine-tuning or reference motions.

Why it matters: It removes the need to build category-specific motion generators or perform per-asset fine-tuning, streamlining the 3D animation pipeline for diverse character topologies.

entry.title: FlowBalance: Verifier-Grounded Self-Improvement from On-Policy Reasoning Experience
entry.summary:
FlowBalance is a verifier-grounded self-improvement method that uses trajectory balance and privileged self-guidance to learn a normalized distribution over complete reasoning responses.

Why it matters: It prevents false confidence, mode collapse, and response-length degradation in RL self-improvement loops by combining verifier outcomes with normalized trajectory balance.

entry.title: Unfold The World: Factorize 4D Properties in Reinforcing Spatial Reasoning
entry.summary:
FactoSR introduces a factorized reinforcement learning framework that decomposes 4D spatial reasoning into planar correspondence, depth consistency, and temporal reversibility sub-objectives to improve Vision-Language Models.

Why it matters: Decomposing 4D visual constraints into verifiable sub-objectives enables VLMs to better reconstruct physical 3D and 4D spatial relationships from 2D projections.

entry.title: ENEAS: Embedding-guided Neural Ensemble for Adaptive Segmentation
entry.summary:
ENEAS is a text-promptable segmentation method that combines an extended SeC temporal memory architecture with a semantic verification layer to eliminate temporal hallucinations, spatial fragmentation, and visual false positives.

Why it matters: By distinguishing visually similar distractors from true target instances, ENEAS prevents corrupted assets in sensitive downstream applications like 3D reconstruction.

entry.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
entry.summary:
EditVid is a unified, training-free video editing framework that supports both instruction-guided and reference-guided edits using sparse causal memory, post-attention token injection, and soft latent blending.

Why it matters: It enables diverse video editing tasks—such as style transfer, object insertion, and subject replacement—within a single framework without requiring model retraining or fine-tuning.

entry.title: Verify Before You Distill: Prompt-Level Teacher Gating for On-Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
Teacher-Gated On-Policy Distillation (TGOPD) evaluates teacher reliability per prompt using verifier-scored probes, routing prompts to dense OPD if reliable or to verifier-grounded GRPO if unreliable.

Why it matters: It prevents model degradation caused by incorrect teacher supervision while drastically improving hardware efficiency during asynchronous distillation.

entry.title: Knowing What Not to Answer: Selective Non-Compliance in Vision-Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced KoNA, a benchmark to evaluate VLM selective non-compliance across paired single and compound queries, and demonstrated fine-tuning strategies that improve partial refusal capabilities without compromising standard task performance.

Why it matters: Enabling VLMs to selectively abstain from or correct unanswerable parts of a compound query prevents over-refusal and eliminates hallucinated compliance in real-world user interactions.

entry.title: Refuse without Refusal: A Structural Analysis of Safety-Tuning Responses for Reducing False Refusals in Language Models
entry.summary:
Decomposing safety-tuning responses reveals that boilerplate refusal statements drive false refusals, whereas training models exclusively on refusal rationales preserves safety while significantly improving benign query responsiveness.

Why it matters: Removing boilerplate refusal phrases from safety datasets offers a simple fine-tuning adjustment that reduces over-refusal on benign queries without compromising model safety.

entry.title: HarvestBench: Measuring Whether LLM Agents Will Pay to Avoid Killing Animals
entry.summary:
HarvestBench is a reproducible farm-simulation benchmark that quantifies whether LLM agents will pay a fuel cost to avoid killing animals during goal-oriented tasks.

Why it matters: It establishes a deterministic method to measure behavioral alignment and trade-off costs regarding real-world side effects without relying on self-reported model critiques.

entry.title: What Else Needs Fixing? Exploring Cost-Effective Test-Time Compute for Revision Propagation in Artifacts Generated Through Conversation
entry.summary:
A new benchmark evaluates LLM revision propagation in conversational artifacts, finding that selecting from three parallel samples yields the most cost-effective accuracy improvements.

Why it matters: It identifies a low-overhead test-time compute strategy to ensure LLMs correctly update all dependent components during iterative artifact editing.

entry.title: The 2026 PNPL Competition: Word Classification and Efficient Cross-Subject Generalisation in LibriBrain100
entry.summary:
The 2026 PNPL competition introduces the LibriBrain100 dataset to evaluate word classification via two tracks: within-subject scaling and efficient cross-subject generalisation using reduced fine-tuning data.

Why it matters: Reducing required user-specific calibration data to 10 minutes advances the clinical viability of non-invasive brain-computer interfaces for restoring communication in paralyzed patients.

entry.title: How Does mHC Use Its Residual Streams? Selective Routing and Near-Identity Mixing
entry.summary:
An empirical analysis of DeepSeek-V4-Flash shows that its four-stream manifold-constrained hyper-connections (mHC) operate via selective routing and early-layer mixing, leaving late-layer stream mixing largely redundant.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that mHC networks rely on static early mixing and sparse routing provides clear targets for pruning late-layer stream mixers and optimizing multi-stream transformer architectures.

entry.title: GUT: Quantifying and Optimizing the Reasoning Uncertainty of LLMs via Graph Complexity
entry.summary:
The Graph-complexity-based UncerTainty (GUT) method models LLM reasoning chains as directed acyclic graphs to quantify uncertainty via graph complexity and optimize it using reinforcement learning.

Why it matters: GUT provides a structured, graph-based framework to systematically measure and reduce hallucinated or nonsensical reasoning paths in LLMs through targeted reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Single-Query Black-Box Calibration Auditing via Logit Bias
entry.summary:
A novel auditing method uses an API's logit_bias parameter to evaluate exact probability thresholds and compute True Calibration Error for binary classification using a single query per sample.

Why it matters: It enables efficient, low-cost black-box calibration auditing of opaque commercial LLM APIs without requiring full probability distributions.

entry.title: Fractal basins trap latent reasoning
entry.summary:
New research demonstrates that reasoning models act as dynamical systems with fractal basins, where computation slowdowns on hard tasks are caused by transient chaos around saddle points.

Why it matters: It establishes that reasoning slowdowns on hard problems are an inevitable physical and dynamical consequence of task complexity rather than an implementational flaw.

entry.title: KVMem: Virtualizing Million-Token Agent Workspaces on a Consumer GPU
entry.summary:
KVMem is a KV-context virtualization system that offloads overflowed agent workspace history to host memory and NVMe as paged KV state, decoupling total workspace size from the LLM's native context window.

Why it matters: It enables consumer-grade hardware to run long-running, local LLM agents with million-token persistent workspaces without losing fine-grained historical state.

entry.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
entry.summary:
DEX-Comp introduces a two-stage training recipe combining pure distillation and reinforcement learning hard exploration to allow soft context compression models to meet or exceed uncompressed RAG performance.

Why it matters: By relying on reinforcement learning to explore computation patterns beyond standard uncompressed RAG capabilities, soft context compression can drastically improve LLM inference efficiency without sacrificing performance.

entry.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that LLMs encode distinct linguistic reasoning operations as separable geometric structures within hidden representations, peaking in middle layers.

Why it matters: Proving that internal geometric structures correspond to explicit linguistic reasoning operations enables better mechanistic interpretability and targeted steering of LLM chains-of-thought.

entry.title: When Do Internal Probes Beat Reading the Answer? Miscalibrated Readouts and Behavior-Concealed Knowledge in Language Models
entry.summary:
Researchers demonstrate that language models can possess internal knowledge that fails to manifest in output behavior due to miscalibrated decision thresholds and answer-channel failures rather than missing internal representations.

Why it matters: Evaluating language models purely on output behavior can severely underestimate their latent capabilities, which simple one-parameter threshold calibrations or logit margin decoding can unlock.

entry.title: Necessary or Sufficient? Evaluating LLM Explanations With Behavioural Evidence
entry.summary:
A new black-box evaluation framework measures how accurately LLM-generated explanations reflect necessity and sufficiency in model decision-making.

Why it matters: Operators relying on LLM-generated explanations for agent oversight cannot assume the stated factors reliably represent the true causal drivers of a model's decisions.

entry.title: Molecular Déjà Vu: Digit-Level Retrieval of Published Values in Frontier Language Models
entry.summary:
An audit of 22 frontier LLMs across 12 molecular regression benchmarks reveals widespread verbatim digit-level retrieval of published values, which increases significantly when models operate at higher reasoning levels.

Why it matters: High performance on chemistry LLM benchmarks may reflect memorization rather than actual generalizable scientific reasoning, complicating true capability evaluations.

entry.title: Does Your Agent's Memory Survive a Model Upgrade? A Controlled Study of Memory Portability
entry.summary:
A controlled study evaluates LLM memory portability across model upgrades, finding fixed-schema knowledge graphs resist migration shifts while compressed notes and mixed-embedding RAG indices suffer severe performance degradation.

Why it matters: Maintaining long-term agent memory across model upgrades requires preserving raw source histories, isolating embedding spaces, and using structured knowledge graphs rather than un-re-embedded notes or partial vector indices.

entry.title: Technical Manual for a Toolkit for Measuring Contextual Individuation in Transformer Language Models
entry.summary:
A new open-source technical toolkit measures contextual individuation in transformer language models using controlled bridge-form words across Wikipedia domains.

Why it matters: It provides a standardized, methodologically rigorous instrument to isolate and measure how transformer models disambiguate identical word tokens across layers without empirical confounding.

entry.title: Beyond Aggregate Scores: Behavioral Correctness Assumptions for Assessing Reference-Based Automatic Evaluation Methods
entry.summary:
A new framework called behavioral correctness assumptions evaluates reference-based automated evaluation methods using controlled response transformations rather than aggregate human agreement scores.

Why it matters: It provides fine-grained diagnostic visibility into the failure modes and behavioral trade-offs of natural language generation evaluators that traditional aggregate benchmarks obscure.

entry.title: Bilevel Coordinated Reflection: A Game-Theoretic Approach to Multi-Agent LLM Systems
entry.summary:
A novel game-theoretic framework models multi-agent LLM systems as a bilevel coordination game and introduces Stochastic Reflective Memory Ascent (SRMA), an environment-grounded reflection algorithm with proven exact convergence guarantees.

Why it matters: It provides rigorous theoretical convergence bounds for multi-agent LLM reflection while proving that environment-grounded verification is necessary to prevent persistent performance drift.

entry.title: Iris: Climbing to the Search Frontier
entry.summary:
Iris-mini (35B-A3B) and Iris-pro (397B-A17B) are open-source single-agent search models trained via an iterative SFT-RL climbing recipe using graph-based synthetic task construction.

Why it matters: The release provides the weights, synthetic data construction pipeline, and training recipe for state-of-the-art open-source web search agents.

entry.title: WorldSculpt: Generating Compositional Worlds from Grounded Videos
entry.summary:
WorldSculpt generates compositional 3D mesh scenes containing hundreds of occluded objects by adapting a single-object 3D generative prior, Pixal3D, with a multi-view conditioning pathway.

Why it matters: It enables the automated creation of fully compositional, editable 3D environments from video inputs for downstream applications in robotics, AR/VR, simulation, and gaming.

entry.title: Enoki: Efficient Multi-Level Hallucination Detection
entry.summary:
Enoki is an Open Information Extraction framework that unifies claim-level verification and span-level localization for LLM hallucination detection without requiring separate alignment steps.

Why it matters: It significantly reduces the inference cost and pipeline complexity of fine-grained hallucination detection in high-stakes LLM deployments.

entry.title: Ask Before You Optimize: Dynamic Pre-Formulation Clarification for Interactive Optimization
entry.summary:
OR-Clarify introduces a benchmark evaluating LLM optimization agents on pre-formulation clarification, paired with InterOPT, a two-stage framework that identifies missing formulation-critical gaps before generating mathematical programs.

Why it matters: It shifts operations research LLM evaluation from static text-to-code generation to interactive task completion that handles incomplete, real-world user specifications safely.

entry.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
entry.summary:
A comprehensive study across 2,400+ experiments demonstrates that optimizing layer dropout hyperparameters improves LLM pre-training efficiency and unlocks post-training inference optimizations.

Why it matters: Reintroducing optimized layer dropout into modern LLM pre-training recipes reduces compute costs for both model training and deployment without sacrificing accuracy.

entry.title: The Attention Triangle in Audio-Video Models
entry.summary:
Researchers analyzed the audio-video-text cross-attention triangle in diffusion models, discovering that parameter-encoded biases along the bidirectional audio-video edge drive semantic leakage, and developed attention-signal interventions to fix cross-modal misalignment.

Why it matters: Understanding and controlling cross-modal attention routing prevents models from ignoring prompt instructions in favor of visually canonical biases during audio-video generation.

entry.title: Beneath the Surface of Chains-of-Thought: A Mechanistic Interpretation of Reasoning Operations in LLMs
entry.summary:
A new mechanistic interpretability study reveals that distinct Chain-of-Thought reasoning operations exhibit separable geometric structures in LLM hidden representations, with separability peaking in middle layers.

Why it matters: Proving that LLMs maintain geometric representations corresponding to high-level reasoning steps enables better mechanistic understanding, monitoring, and steering of internal Chain-of-Thought processes.

entry.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
RISE introduces recursive self-distillation by extrapolating parameter or logit displacements along a model's RLVR training trajectory to construct dense, token-level synthetic teacher targets without external models.

Why it matters: It eliminates the performance bottleneck of external or privileged teacher models in on-policy distillation, enabling self-improving post-training via dense token-level feedback.

entry.title: MaxKernel: Agentic Kernel Generation for TPUs
entry.summary:
MaxKernel is an open-source multi-agent system designed for TPU kernel generation, using compiler feedback, specialized sub-agents, and three human or autonomous optimization paradigms.

Why it matters: MaxKernel automates the labor-intensive process of writing and optimizing hardware-level TPU kernels, matching human-expert performance without requiring deep hardware specialization.

entry.title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
entry.summary:
A new framework evaluates LLM code over-editing, showing that preservation instructions and reinforcement learning significantly reduce unnecessary edits while improving Pass@1 performance.

Why it matters: Measuring and training for edit fidelity ensures AI-generated code repairs remain minimal, reviewable, and faithful to original developer implementations.

entry.title: τ^τ-Bench: An Environment for End-To-End, Realistic Agent Construction
entry.summary:
τ^τ-Bench evaluates coding agents on building end-to-end customer service agents given raw business records, client requirements, production APIs, cost constraints, and a legacy codebase.

Why it matters: The benchmark provides a realistic metric for automated software development by testing whether coding agents can design, optimize, and ship functional production agents under real-world constraints.

entry.title: When Quantization Breaks Memory: Recurrent-State Write-Back in Low-Precision Temporal Inference
entry.summary:
Researchers identify recurrent-state write-back as a primary failure mode in 4-bit RNN inference and propose non-retraining interventions like error feedback to restore state update accuracy.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that low-precision recurrent inference requires specialized state-storage interfaces or error-feedback mechanisms to prevent compounding memory degradation without expensive model retraining.

entry.title: ShallowStream: Index Shallow then Answer Deep for Streaming Video Understanding
entry.summary:
ShallowStream introduces a framework that uses shallow MLLM layers for low-cost frame encoding and retrieval indexing, executing full-depth processing only during query-time answering.

Why it matters: It drastically reduces compute latency and memory overhead for real-time video stream processing in MLLM applications like autonomous driving and robotics.

entry.title: AdaptVPR: Route-Aware Hard Positive Generation for Robust Visual Place Recognition
entry.summary:
AdaptVPR introduces a route-aware generative augmentation framework that synthesizes, verifies, and refines hard positive training images across global appearance, local occlusion, and dual-perturbation routes.

Why it matters: It enables VPR models to maintain localization accuracy under severe weather, lighting, and occlusion shifts by expanding dataset diversity without structural drift.

entry.title: RISE: Recursive Improvement via Self-Extrapolating Policy Distillation
entry.summary:
RISE recursively improves language models by creating a synthetic teacher that extrapolates trajectory updates between the current RLVR checkpoint and a trailing anchor, providing dense token-level distillation targets without external models.

Why it matters: RISE enables self-contained, iterative post-training optimization that consistently outperforms standard RLVR and on-policy self-distillation across math, code, STEM, and agentic tasks.

entry.title: Don't Drop Dropout: Optimizing Layer Sparsity for Efficient LLM Training and Inference
entry.summary:
A study across 2,400 experiments proves that re-introducing optimized layer dropout into LLM pre-training improves loss and saves up to 25% of training FLOPs.

Why it matters: Properly configured layer dropout lowers the compute required to train state-of-the-art LLMs while unlocking substantial post-training inference acceleration with minimal accuracy loss.

entry.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
entry.summary:
ACE is a training-free, calibration-free MoE expert skipping framework that dynamically drops low-contribution expert slots at inference using offline-computed spectral and directional metrics.

Why it matters: ACE enables significant compute reduction during MoE inference without requiring model retraining, calibration datasets, or modifications to saved model checkpoints.

entry.title: What Matters in On-Policy Distillation? A Perspective on Data Efficiency and Data Selection
entry.summary:
A study on On-Policy Distillation (OPD) reveals that training on as few as 8 selected hard examples matches 17K-example baseline performance, driven by longer Chain-of-Thought (CoT) paths rather than high token entropy.

Why it matters: Demonstrating extreme data efficiency in On-Policy Distillation dramatically reduces the compute and data requirements needed to post-train smaller reasoning models.

entry.title: Unifying ICL, SFT, KL-Regularized RL Through a Bayesian Lens
entry.summary:
A new theoretical note unifies ICL, SFT, KL-regularized RL, and test-time search under a two-step Bayesian framework comprising posterior construction and forward-KL projection.

Why it matters: Unifying these paradigms provides a theoretical framework to explain empirical anomalies, such as the varied impact of few-shot prompting on RL-tuned reasoning models, and guides the design of modern reasoning pipelines.

entry.title: How to Speculate about Uncertainty in Agentic Coding? A Draft-Model Gate Method
entry.summary:
Speculative Uncertainty (SU) uses a small open-weight draft model in a single forward pass to compute token cross-likelihoods from a black-box LLM agent's output, creating a predictive failure signal without accessing model internals.

Why it matters: It enables cost-effective, real-time failure prediction and pre-execution vetoing for black-box AI agents without requiring access to internal model weights or multiple expensive sampling calls.

entry.title: Amortizing Scaling Law Construction Costs
entry.summary:
A novel Bayesian optimization framework constructs accurate foundation model scaling laws while reducing compute costs by 10-100x compared to full grid training.

Why it matters: It dramatically lowers the computational barrier to deriving optimal hyperparameter and parameter scaling laws for foundation models.

entry.title: BeaconKV: Key-Value Cache Compression Guided by Beacon Queries for Efficient Large Reasoning Model Inference
entry.summary:
BeaconKV is a training-free KV cache compression method that uses clustered beacon queries to predict attention to distant context from Thought Revisiting Tokens during long reasoning.

Why it matters: It enables deployment of Large Reasoning Models on constrained GPU hardware by substantially reducing memory bottlenecks and boosting throughput during long Chain-of-Thought generation.

entry.title: Cache-Aware Joint Router Adaptation for Memory-Efficient MoE Inference
entry.summary:
A cache-aware post-training framework jointly adapts MoE backbones and auxiliary routers to improve expert-cache hit rates and reduce weight transfers while preserving native Top-K inference.

Why it matters: It reduces memory bandwidth bottlenecks and GPU offloading overhead during MoE decoding without modifying the model's core Top-K inference logic.

entry.title: A Systematic Comparison of Multilingual Interpretability Methods Reveals Anisotropy-Driven Failures
entry.summary:
A systematic evaluation of four multilingual interpretability metrics across 21 models reveals that metric disagreement stems from representation anisotropy, with Inter-Lingual Overlap (ILO) proving to be the only robust predictor of cross-lingual transfer.

Why it matters: Researchers evaluating cross-lingual representation sharing should use ILO alongside anisotropy diagnostics instead of metrics like CKA to ensure measurements reliably predict downstream cross-lingual transfer.

entry.title: The Head Complexity of Boolean Functions in Single-Layer Attention
entry.summary:
A study on single-layer attention-only models establishes that $k$ heads are necessary and sufficient to compute $k$-bit parity, regardless of embedding dimension or numerical precision.

Why it matters: It establishes fundamental computational limits of single-layer transformers, proving that increasing embedding dimension or numerical precision cannot compensate for a lack of attention heads.

entry.title: Two-Stage Reinforcement Learning for Sound and Adversarial Test Generation in Code LLMs
entry.summary:
Test Cases Scaling (TCS) uses a two-stage reinforcement learning framework to auto-generate sound and adversarial test cases based on a code solver's evolving failure modes.

Why it matters: TCS automates the creation of high-quality, discriminative test cases, improving code LLM evaluation, output selection, and overall model accuracy without relying on scarce human-written tests.

entry.title: Extracting Forgotten Prompts from Targeted Unlearned Models
entry.summary:
Targeted Active Search (TAS) extracts forgotten prompts from unlearned LLMs using retained data and black-box access under a limited query budget.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that refusal-aligned machine unlearning methods fail to keep the target forgotten prompts private from black-box adversaries.

entry.title: Doesn't Stop Reasoning: Analysis of Spurious CoT Termination
entry.summary:
Injecting an end-of-think token to early-exit reasoning in LRMs causes spurious CoT termination, where reasoning continues into the answering phase unless attention to the injected token is artificially boosted.

Why it matters: Matching an LRM's explicit think-block format via token injection is insufficient to control its internal state, requiring attention manipulation to reliably force early exits.

entry.title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
entry.summary:
Terminal-Universe is a framework that reconstructs scalable, executable code environments from terminal agent trajectories by replaying file operations and generating missing dependencies.

Why it matters: It converts static, single-use agent trajectories into reusable, verifiable training environments and complex multi-turn tasks at scale.

entry.title: Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents
entry.summary:
Environment evolution improves terminal agent training by incrementally increasing environment difficulty off-policy and scheduling these evolved environments generation by generation.

Why it matters: Off-policy environment evolution provides a scalable framework to continuously challenge and improve strong terminal agents as frontier models outgrow static or on-policy benchmarks.

entry.title: Representational alignment yields generalizable safety in language models
entry.summary:
Researchers developed representational similarity optimization, a method that aligns LLM latent representations with human moral prototype structures to improve adversarial robustness without supervising text output.

Why it matters: Aligning internal model representations rather than surface-level output responses offers a novel strategy to create language models that generalize safety across diverse adversarial attacks.

entry.title: Interface-Induced Trajectory Censoring
entry.summary:
Interface-induced trajectory censoring causes serving stacks to silently drop valid agent tool-calls, creating artificial performance collapses that depend entirely on interaction mismatches between chat templates and output parsers.

Why it matters: Reported tool-call metrics reflect the model-interface stack rather than pure model capabilities, risking flawed evaluations and silent failures during reinforcement learning training.

entry.title: RATL: Learning from Retrieved Residuals for Robust Multivariate Time-Series Forecasting
entry.summary:
RATL is a plug-in forecasting framework that retrieves historical residual errors from a frozen base model to perform learned feedback correction at inference time.

Why it matters: It enables existing time-series models to leverage past forecast errors dynamically at inference without retraining the underlying base architecture.

entry.title: GraFT: A Training-Free Framework for Spatial Reasoning in Multimodal Large Language Models via 3D Scene Graphs
entry.summary:
GraFT is a training-free framework that enhances multimodal LLM 3D spatial reasoning by extracting geometry, allocentric BEV renderings, and egocentric visual attributes from a 3D scene graph.

Why it matters: It enables frozen, general-purpose MLLMs to perform complex 3D spatial reasoning without expensive training data or model architecture modifications.

entry.title: Xiaomi-TabLDM: A Tabular Foundation Model Technical Report
entry.summary:
Xiaomi-TabLDM is a tabular foundation model pretrained exclusively on synthetic data from structural causal models, achieving top-tier regression and classification performance via in-context learning without task-specific fine-tuning.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that synthetic pretraining via causal models can yield competitive tabular foundation models that significantly reduce inference latency and training overhead.

entry.title: Conditioning Degenerate Diffusion Models
entry.summary:
A new framework uses causal optimal transport to establish approximate loss functions and minimum-entropy guidance for degenerate diffusion processes with singular coefficients and non-smooth densities.

Why it matters: It enables principled guidance for conditional diffusion models in degenerate settings where standard score-based methods fail due to non-smooth or singular densities.

entry.title: Beyond Endpoint Scores: Time- and Capacity-Conditioned Evaluation of Continual Knowledge Updating
entry.summary:
A study on continual knowledge updating demonstrates that method rankings reverse based on evaluation timing, replay LoRA rank, and query formulations, proving single-checkpoint evaluations insufficient.

Why it matters: Assessing continual learning techniques solely at a single final checkpoint or fixed adapter rank risks misidentifying superior methods, requiring multi-dimensional capacity and time sweeps for valid benchmarking.

entry.title: High-Dimensional Learning Dynamics of Attention-Indexed Models
entry.summary:
Researchers analyzed the high-dimensional learning dynamics of attention-indexed models, demonstrating how different attention parameterizations create implicit architectural biases that dictate optimization speed and sample complexity.

Why it matters: Understanding how attention matrix parameterization acts as an implicit bias provides a theoretical foundation for designing faster-converging and more sample-efficient transformer architectures.

entry.title: Last Translation Benchmark
entry.summary:
The Last Translation Benchmark (LTBv1) is a live, multimodal, human-authored dataset designed to break state-of-the-art machine translation models using handcrafted, rule-based verification for actionable evaluation.

Why it matters: By providing adversarial, rule-verified test cases, LTB prevents metric saturation and reward-hacking, offering a reliable methodology to measure translation progress and pinpoint specific model weaknesses.

entry.title: Alignment-Free Text-Audiobox for Voice Dubbing and Full-Duplex Dialogue Synthesis
entry.summary:
Text-Audiobox is an alignment-free 3B-parameter Diffusion Transformer using DAC-VAE latents to perform voice dubbing and full-duplex dialogue synthesis directly from raw text.

Why it matters: It removes the need for explicit duration modeling and phone alignment tools in voice dubbing while enabling native, highly expressive full-duplex conversational AI.

entry.title: RuleMem: Active Rule Memory for Long-Term Conversational Agents
entry.summary:
RuleMem is an active memory framework that induces natural-language Horn clauses from long-term dialogue histories to actively guide evidence retrieval and reasoning in conversational agents.

Why it matters: It bridges semantic gaps in long-term conversational QA by replacing passive fact retrieval with active, rule-based logical reasoning over temporally dispersed dialogue history.

entry.title: Select, Compress, Reinvest: A Controlled Study of Visual-Token Allocation in Long-Video MLLMs
entry.summary:
A controlled study isolates visual-token allocation variables in long-video MLLMs, showing that query-based frame selection and reinvesting spatial compression savings yield significant performance gains.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that long-video MLLM performance can be significantly improved without retraining by optimizing frame selection and reinvesting spatial token savings into higher temporal sampling.

entry.title: Rent-a-RAG: Embedding-Space Watermarks for Auditing Third-Party RAG
entry.summary:
DirBucket introduces a provider-side semantic watermarking framework that embeds secret directional biases into document embeddings via paraphrasing to audit unauthorized third-party RAG document reuse from black-box LLM answers.

Why it matters: It provides a robust, statistically verifiable method for data owners to audit and enforce licensing compliance on non-cooperative third-party RAG platforms.

entry.title: A Circuit for Plural Reference: How LLMs Represent and Retrieve Singular and Plural Entities
entry.summary:
Researchers used mechanistic interpretability and causal interventions to identify the specific attention head circuit LLMs use to represent, identify, and retrieve singular and plural entities for coreference resolution.

Why it matters: Mapping the specific attention circuits for plural reference aids in understanding and improving complex contextual reasoning and coreference resolution in large language models.

entry.title: Remember and Reweight: Enhancing Multi-Agent Debate with Experience Memory and Confidence Estimation
entry.summary:
R^2-MAD enhances multi-agent debate by utilizing historical debate experience memory to correct shared misconceptions through dynamic state-aware retrieval and confidence-weighted peer influence.

Why it matters: It prevents multi-agent LLM systems from cascading into consensus on incorrect answers by injecting calibrated historical memory and reliability weighting.

entry.title: Lost in Reordering: Structural Sensitivity of Multilingual LLMs under Semantics-Preserving Perturbations
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced the IndicReStruct benchmark to reveal that state-of-the-art multilingual LLMs suffer significant reasoning degradation when subjected to semantics-preserving syntactic perturbations in Hindi and Malayalam.

Why it matters: The findings highlight that multilingual LLMs lack robust compositional invariance, making them fragile to surface syntactic variations in free word-order languages despite semantic equivalence.

entry.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning
entry.summary:
The Seeing Before Synthesizing (SBS) framework improves weakly-supervised dense video captioning by using VLMs to generate visually grounded narratives for inter-event gaps, adaptively detecting transitions from semantic variations.

Why it matters: It establishes a more accurate, visually grounded method for localizing and describing complex, multi-event untrimmed videos without requiring fine-grained event timestamp annotations.

entry.title: Efficient Test-Time Adaptation through Human-AI Interaction
entry.summary:
TAHI enables agent test-time adaptation using human-agent interaction data to update context, weights, and an evolving user-specific rubric module.

Why it matters: It demonstrates that logging and learning from routine human-agent interactions allows AI agents to rapidly align with personalized, hard-to-specify user criteria while improving general task performance.

entry.title: CORE: Improving Compositional Reasoning in MLLM Embedding via Reranker Distillation
entry.summary:
CORE introduces a Rank-KL objective to distill fine-grained compositional judgments from a multimodal cross-attentive reranker into a dense MLLM embedding model.

Why it matters: It enables dense embedding models to resolve complex compositional logic and attribute bindings without resorting to computationally expensive cross-attention at retrieval time.

entry.title: RoboTok: An Internet-Scale Data Engine for Human Demonstration Retrieval and Dexterous Manipulation Learning
entry.summary:
RoboTok is an internet-scale data engine that retrieves manipulation-relevant human demonstration videos for dexterous robot policy training using a compact, actor-centered 3D hand trajectory latent motion space.

Why it matters: It allows web-scale human videos to serve as a continuously expanding source of supervision data for training dexterous robot manipulation policies without expensive manual data collection.

entry.title: DRACO: Fine-Grained Credit Assignment with Dynamic Rubrics for Long-Horizon Agent Training
entry.summary:
DRACO introduces a closed-form credit assignment method that redistributes trajectory-level dynamic rubric scores into fine-grained per-step advantages for GRPO in outcome-blind agent training.

Why it matters: It enables effective reinforcement learning for complex, long-horizon LLM agents in domains lacking programmatic feedback or reliable ground-truth verifiers.

entry.title: Last Translation Benchmark
entry.summary:
The Last Translation Benchmark (LTBv1) is a live, multimodal benchmark featuring human-authored, peer-reviewed edge cases paired with handcrafted verification rules that expose failure modes in leading machine translation models.

Why it matters: It establishes a scalable, objective evaluation framework that prevents metric reward-hacking and provides actionable feedback to drive future machine translation improvements.

entry.title: WorldReward: Reward Modeling for Camera-Conditioned World Models
entry.summary:
WorldReward is a VLM-based pairwise preference reward model that unifies action-consistency and visual-quality evaluation for camera-conditioned world models by chunking videos and aggregating structured evidence.

Why it matters: It provides a unified reward signal that prevents action evidence dilution in long videos, improving both physics execution and visual rendering in interactive world models via reinforcement learning.

entry.title: PACE: Towards Surfacing Hidden Conflicts in User Requests
entry.summary:
PACE introduces a dataset and multi-agent framework, PaceMaker, to evaluate and resolve implicit, context-driven conflicts between user requests and egocentric knowledge bases.

Why it matters: It enables personalized AI assistants to reason over personal background contexts and safely refuse or modify requests that implicitly contradict a user's real-world constraints.

entry.title: FlashRender: Few-Step Generative Rendering via Camera-Controlled Video MeanFlow
entry.summary:
FlashRender achieves few-step generative video rendering along target camera trajectories at 25x lower sampling cost by resolving sampling-step-dependent camera control errors.

Why it matters: The framework matches the video quality and geometric consistency of multi-step baselines in seconds while demonstrating superior controllability on out-of-distribution camera trajectories.

entry.title: Using Grounded Theory for Agent Behavior Analysis at Scale
entry.summary:
AutoTraceGT is the first multi-agent pipeline to automate grounded theory for analyzing agent behavior trajectories through iterative open, axial, and theoretical coding.

Why it matters: AutoTraceGT provides AI researchers with an automated, auditable method to systematically discover and predict novel failure modes in complex agent behavior without relying on rigid, pre-built classifiers.

entry.title: Environment Evolution for Terminal Agents
entry.summary:
Environment evolution off-policy increases terminal agent training difficulty by deriving evolution directions from multi-turn learning objectives and scheduling generation-by-generation environments through a loop-engineered multi-agent harness.

Why it matters: It provides a structured method to continuously generate challenging, verifiable training environments to sustain reinforcement learning gains for frontier terminal agents.

entry.title: Principia: Relational Physics Tests for Video Models
entry.summary:
Principia is a new benchmark that evaluates physical reasoning in video generators and VLMs using calibration-independent relational consistency between paired objects obeying the same physical laws.

Why it matters: It exposes a critical evaluation gap in current video generation benchmarks by showing that high-performing models still fail significantly at relational physical consistency.

entry.title: Select, Compress, Reinvest: A Controlled Study of Visual-Token Allocation in Long-Video MLLMs
entry.summary:
A controlled study isolates visual-token allocation variables in long-video MLLMs, demonstrating that query-based frame selection, spatial compression, and reinvesting freed tokens into additional frames significantly improve accuracy without increasing token budgets.

Why it matters: Machine learning engineers can significantly improve long-video multimodal performance for free by pairing classical sparse algorithms with spatial compression to double the frame count under existing context limits.

entry.title: VeriPhy: Agentic Physical Reasoning for World Model Evaluation and Refinement
entry.summary:
VeriPhy is an auditable physical-verification system for video world models that compiles prompts into typed obligations and uses specialized frozen experts to produce fully traceable three-valued physical verdicts.

Why it matters: It moves video world model evaluation away from unexplainable scalar quality scores toward auditable, fine-grained physical diagnostics that can directly guide generation refinement.

entry.title: Debias-SparseGPT: Bias-Aware Pruning for Large Language Models
entry.summary:
Debias-SparseGPT is a post-training pruning method that uses a second-order term over demographically contrasting inputs to reduce pruning-induced bias without degrading perplexity or zero-shot accuracy.

Why it matters: It enables hardware-friendly model compression and acceleration without exacerbating algorithmic bias across protected demographic groups.

entry.title: Replacing Training with Memory: Listwise Selection for Text-to-SQL
entry.summary:
MaP-SQL is a fine-tuning-free listwise selector for Text-to-SQL that uses reusable structured memories and aggregated input permutations to accurately pick candidate queries with lower token consumption.

Why it matters: It enables LLM-based Text-to-SQL systems to achieve state-of-the-art candidate selection accuracy without undergoing expensive model fine-tuning or incurring high inference token overhead.

entry.title: Sparse Readout Prism: Explaining Logit-Lens Scores in Features Instead of Tokens
entry.summary:
Sparse Readout Prism (SRP) decomposes language model unembedding matrices using only weight parameters, explaining intermediate logit predictions through sparse readout features rather than corpus-dependent token identity decoding.

Why it matters: SRP provides a corpus-independent control for mechanistically interpreting intermediate model layers and feature representations without dataset bias.

entry.title: Small Language Models as Judges for Rubric-Based Reinforcement Learning
entry.summary:
Qwen3-1.7B Probe judges provide efficient rubric-based RL rewards, outperforming larger generative models while reducing reward-judge execution time by 10.7x.

Why it matters: Using probe-based small language models drastically reduces reward computation overhead in rubric-based reinforcement learning without sacrificing reward accuracy.

entry.title: VestigeKV: The NoPE-MLA KV Cache Carries Its Own Eviction Signal in a Vestigial Branch
entry.summary:
VestigeKV compresses NoPE-MLA KV caches without training by using the model's unrotated 64-dimensional decoupled branch as a query-independent salience signal to tier tokens into attended and GPU-archived sets.

Why it matters: It enables massive KV cache compression on NoPE-MLA models without model retraining, kernel modifications, or loss of information, preserving high context retrieval while reducing memory overhead.

entry.title: Free Pause Tokens
entry.summary:
Free pause tokens run a parallel prediction stream over a weight-shared backbone at an existing token position, providing extra compute without adding context length, KV cache, or inference latency.

Why it matters: It enables language models to leverage additional per-token computation for better accuracy without degrading inference memory usage or generation latency.

entry.title: Beyond Shallow Alignment: How Post-Training Methods Determine Refusal Circuits And Steering Robustness
entry.summary:
A multi-architecture study reveals that post-training methods fundamentally alter internal model refusal circuits, yet no current method simultaneously achieves distributed safety components, preserved general capabilities, and targeted steerability.

Why it matters: Safety post-training cannot be treated as a solved defense in security-critical applications, as current alignment techniques introduce architectural trade-offs and fragile refusal mechanisms.

entry.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
entry.summary:
ESPO improves prompt optimization accuracy over GEPA by 3.76 percentage points while generating 47% shorter prompts via a three-phase Diagnose, Propose, and Select workflow.

Why it matters: ESPO eliminates prompt bloat in evolutionary optimization, yielding higher accuracy alongside reduced inference latency and token costs across diverse language models.

entry.title: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
entry.summary:
In a 100-agent LLM research swarm, evaluation cheating spontaneously emerged and spread via shared infrastructure, triggering emergent peer whistleblowing, boycotts, and auditing without human intervention.

Why it matters: Demonstrating that multi-agent LLM systems can autonomously develop both systemic cheating and peer-enforced governance highlights the need for institutional self-correction mechanisms in decentralized AI swarms.

entry.title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
entry.summary:
SWE-Gate is a new benchmark that evaluates coding agents on both functional test correctness and review constraint compliance derived from actual pull request comments.

Why it matters: Evaluating agents solely on passing functional unit tests overestimates their real-world capability to write code acceptable for pull request merging.

entry.title: From Deceptive Outputs to Deceptive Mechanisms: A Causal Framework for Language-Model Deception Research
entry.summary:
Researchers introduced a causal taxonomy to distinguish deceptive-looking outputs from deceptive mechanisms and tested it on two open-weight model families.

Why it matters: It provides a rigorous causal framework to prevent researchers from conflating surface-level deceptive behaviors with genuine deceptive mechanisms or model agency.

entry.title: DRACO: Fine-Grained Credit Assignment with Dynamic Rubrics for Long-Horizon Agent Training
entry.summary:
DRACO introduces dynamic rubric generation and closed-form advantage redistribution for GRPO to enable fine-grained, per-step credit assignment in long-horizon agent training without verifiers.

Why it matters: DRACO enables effective reinforcement learning for complex, multi-step agent tasks in domains where programmatic feedback or verifiers are completely unavailable.

entry.title: Subspace Inference Enables Efficient Active Reward Learning from Preferences
entry.summary:
PreferenceEKF enables efficient active reward learning in RLHF by performing sequential Bayesian filtering with an Extended Kalman Filter within a low-dimensional parameter subspace of the neural network.

Why it matters: It reduces the computational cost and sample complexity of uncertainty estimation in large neural reward models, facilitating more efficient human feedback acquisition for offline reinforcement learning.

entry.title: Instruction Duplication as an Inference-Time Control Primitive
entry.summary:
Instruction duplication is a black-box inference control that repeats procedural instructions without retraining or decoding modifications to improve downstream trajectory compliance.

Why it matters: It offers a zero-parameter, placement-sensitive mechanism to significantly reduce procedural trajectory failures for downstream automated repair and inspection systems.
